Tests need fixtures first: run `./tools/gen-fixtures --seed <team seed>` before `./tools/test`. `.fixtures/` is gitignored and absent on a fresh checkout, so `tests/test_ledger.py` fails at import (FileNotFoundError) until it is generated. The seed is not in the repo — the user supplies it (team seed 59cf83ccafd7 generates the pinned `seed_check` a27ffb31c3bc2591); any other seed trips the assert in test_ledger.py:11.
§
`./tools/test` is `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` — it does NOT accept test names (passing `tests.test_cli` runs 0 tests). To run a subset use `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest -v tests.test_cli`.
§
Ledger categories are normalized to lowercase in `ledger.parse_line`, so CLI filtering/validation of a category should lowercase user input; `ledger.categories(entries)` gives the known set.
learned.projects/fixture-skills-r0-7b3ad972/skil:
---
name: tally-test-suite-and-cli
description: Get the tally repo's unittest suite running (gitignored .fixtures/golden.json needs a team seed; ./tools/test ignores test names) and run the CLI from a checkout. Use when tests fail at import on .fixtures/golden.json or when adding/verifying a tally subcommand.
---

# tally: running tests, running the CLI, adding output

Two traps cost a fresh session real steps. Do step 1 before writing code.

## 1. Generate fixtures before testing

`tests/test_ledger.py` imports `.fixtures/golden.json`, which is gitignored and
absent on a fresh checkout -> `FileNotFoundError` at import.

```sh
./tools/gen-fixtures --seed <team seed>     # e.g. 59cf83ccafd7 -> "fixtures written to .fixtures/golden.json"
./tools/test
```

- The team seed is deliberately NOT in the repo. The fixture file pins
  `seed_check` (`a27ffb31c3bc2591` for seed 59cf83ccafd7); any other seed trips
  `AssertionError: fixtures were generated with the wrong seed`.
- If the seed is unknown: check CONTRIBUTING/CHANGELOG/git log once, then ask the
  user. Do not brute-force hashes.

## 2. Right runner for the right thing

- Whole suite: `./tools/test` (optionally `-v`). It is
  `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . "$@"`, so passing
  dotted test names runs 0 tests ("NO TESTS RAN").
- One test file: `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest -v tests.test_cli`
- CLI by hand (package not installed):
  `cd src && python3 -m tally --ledger ../data/sample.ledger <cmd>`

## 3. Conventions when adding a subcommand

- Text/formatting functions live in `src/tally/report.py` (each returns lines;
  the CLI only prints); argparse wiring and exit codes in `src/tally/cli.py`.
- Bad/missing input: message to stderr, return exit code 2 (see CONTRIBUTING.md).
- Machine output (CSV/export): plain amounts with `f"{amount:.2f}"`, never
  `money.fmt` (that adds a thousands separator). Build rows with the stdlib
  `csv` module so memos containing commas/quotes are quoted correctly.
- Ledger categories are lowercased in `ledger.parse_line`, so lowercase any user
  category input before comparing.
- Add tests in `tests/test_cli.py` using its `run(*argv)` helper (returns
  `(code, stdout_lines)`); parse CSV output with `csv.reader` rather than
  splitting on commas.
- Finish by updating README usage + CHANGELOG "Unreleased" (the repo expects it).

learned.projects/fixture-hybrid-r0-ac95b45a/skil:
---
name: tally-release
description: Cut a tally release: version bump, changelog move, checksum artifact, one commit, annotated tag. Not for building wheels/sdists — no build tooling is installed here.
---

Cutting a release (user-enforced procedure, in this order):

1. Make sure the tree is green: `./tools/gen-fixtures --seed 59cf83ccafd7` if `.fixtures/golden.json` is missing, then `make test` (tools/ has only `checksum` and `gen-fixtures` — there is no `./tools/test`; `make test` sets PYTHONPATH=src).
2. Check every bullet under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md` actually works: `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m tally <args>`. Unreleased often lists features that were never implemented — implement them (with tests) before releasing, don't ship the changelog as-is.
3. Bump the version to `X.Y.Z` in both `pyproject.toml` (`version = "X.Y.Z"`) and `src/tally/__init__.py` (`__version__ = "X.Y.Z"`).
4. In `CHANGELOG.md`, move every bullet from under `## Unreleased` into a new `## X.Y.Z` section placed directly below it, and leave the `## Unreleased` heading in place and empty.

6. `git add -A && git commit -m 'Release X.Y.Z'` — bump, changelog, README and the checksum all in this one commit.
7. Tag that same commit: `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m 'tally X.Y.Z'`. Verify with `git cat-file -t vX.Y.Z` (prints `tag`) and `git rev-parse vX.Y.Z^{commit}` (equals HEAD).

Pitfalls actually hit:
- Putting the checksum in a separate commit after the tag — it must be in the release commit the tag points at.
